content.text: {"label":"outage","explanation":"A P1 incident (INC-20261006-6998) opened at 10:31 reports UPI transactions failing with timeout errors because switch-to-NPCI connectivity is degraded. In the 10:30 interval, payments volume jumped to 213 calls against 111.9 forecast (+90%), and service level fell to 4.7% with 59 abandoned calls. upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. payment_status_enquiry is 1.44x and refund_status 1.16x, both consistent with customers chasing failed payments. Staffing is close to plan: agents on phones are near planned, and absences are at or near usual levels, so this is not a supply problem. The marketing calendar is empty. General is also up 30% with SL at 54.5%, likely partly spillover, so it cannot donate agents.","plan_name":"UPI outage containment: payments known-issue IVR, chat deflection, breaks, coaching and overtime","rationale":"The demand is incident-driven, so the first step is to cut it at source. A known-issue IVR message on payments covers the rising UPI failure and payment-status reasons and should stop about 20% of those callers. Chat deflection then moves up to 20% of payment_status_enquiry and refund_status calls to chat at Rs 12 per chat. Moving cross-skilled agents is ruled out because general is at 54.5% SL, below the 70% floor a donor queue must keep. To get capacity quickly, I delay breaks by 45 min on both queues and cancel non-mandatory coaching through the early afternoon. Overtime covers the gap until the outage is fixed, as two consecutive 2-hour offers on payments. The first offers 15 agents (about 6 accept, roughly Rs 4,320); the second offers 10 (about 4 accept, roughly Rs 2,880). That is about Rs 7,200 in total, well inside the Rs 15,000 daily budget and leaving room to add more if the incident drags on.
